====== Start a business in Virginia (LLC filing path) ======

**Virginia · How do I start a business?** · state model checked by Claude · quality 1.00

//Generated by [[https://github.com/alibama/lexflow|lexflow]] from the state statutes (open-us-law, government publisher text) and checked by Claude: every quoted phrase was matched word for word against the statute text, and the process passed the BPMN/DMN schemas, bpmnlint and a Petri-net soundness check. Information, not legal advice.//

**Governing law:** [[https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/13.1-1011/|Va. Code Ann. § 13.1-1011]] — Articles of organization

  <bpmn:collaboration id="collab_va_business" name="Start a business in Virginia (LLC filing path)">
    <bpmn:documentation textFormat="text/plain">Someone wants to start a business, here as a limited liability company</bpmn:documentation>
    <bpmn:extensionElements>
      <lex:model id="va-business" jurisdiction="va" jurisdictionName="Virginia" reviewStatus="draft" method="gold-manual">
        <lex:gap>Only the LLC filing path is modelled step by step (articles of organization under § 13.1-1011). The other filed structures do not all follow it: a limited partnership is formed when the Commission files its certificate and admits it to record (§ 50-73.11 C, § 50-73.17 A.5), with no certificate issued; a partnership becomes an LLP when its statement of registration is filed, and the Commission must register any partnership that submits a completed statement with the fee (§ 50-73.132 A, B). Only corporations follow a certificate-issuance pattern like the LLC's (§§ 13.1-621, 13.1-820, not printed here). Their content and compliance checks are not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>State formation is only half of starting a business: most Virginia localities also require a local business licence (BPOL) under their own ordinances, authorised by Va. Code § 58.1-3700 et seq. Fee caps by population are in § 58.1-3703 A; the licence itself and its tax rates come from the local ordinance, which is scored separately.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>§ 59.1-69 applies to any 'person' (§ 1-230), so it reaches entities trading under a name other than their own, not just sole proprietors. The certificate's contents (§ 59.1-70 A) are cited, not checked step by step.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>The local licence is one step (local_license), issued by the commissioner of the revenue (§ 59.1-74 B; see also § 58.1-3703 E) for the fee the locality's governing body may charge (§ 58.1-3703 A). It is reached by either of two exclusive paths that rejoin: directly after the certificate is recorded, or, for a company trading under an assumed name, only after the certificate of assumed name is filed and evidence of the filing given to the commissioner of the revenue (§ 59.1-74 B). The evidence is modelled only where the locality requires a licence, since the statute makes it a precondition of the licence and requires it nowhere else; a trade-name company in a locality without a licence ends at llc_exists after filing its certificate. The choice after recordation is not mutually exclusive: a company with an assumed name in a locality that requires a licence satisfies both uses_assumed_name and locality_requires_license. The model is correct only if the exclusive gateway evaluates its branches in the order written (uses_assumed_name first), as BPMN engines that follow document order do; an engine that picked the direct licence branch would issue the licence without the assumed-name filing that § 59.1-74 B requires first. The flow conditions take one variable per step, so the direct branch cannot be guarded by 'not uses_assumed_name' without also blocking the trade-name branch, which reaches the same step. The second locality_requires_license gateway after the evidence is always true there. On every path the LLC already exists from issuance (§ 13.1-1004 B).</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>The nonstock corporation sections printed (§ 13.1-815.1, § 13.1-816) are the versions 'effective until January 1, 2027'; the replacement versions were not in the corpus and should be checked after that date.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Nonstock status is a state corporate form, not tax exemption; federal 501(c) status is outside the Code of Virginia and not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Professionals are not required to use a professional entity: §§ 13.1-542.1 and 13.1-1101.1 also allow ordinary corporations and LLCs unless other law or regulation prohibits it. Architects, engineers and land surveyors have extra ownership rules (§ 13.1-549, § 13.1-1111). Professional entities do not shield a professional's own professional liability (see §§ 13.1-547 and 13.1-1109, not printed here).</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>A limited partner who participates in control of the business can lose the shield toward people who reasonably believe he is a general partner (§ 50-73.24 A); not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Annual registration fees and continuation reports (e.g. § 13.1-1062 for LLCs, $50 LLP annual continuation report in § 50-73.83 F.2) are not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>A delayed effective date for the certificate (subsection D of § 13.1-1004) is not modelled.</lex:gap>

    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>

===== Steps and the words they come from =====

  - **Sign and deliver articles of organization** — Organizer (founder) · //permission// (§ 13.1-1010) \\ “//signing and delivering articles of organization to the Commission for filing//”
  - **Collect the $100 filing fee** — State Corporation Commission · //obligation// (§ 13.1-1005(1)) \\ “//For filing any one of the following, the fee shall be $100//”
  - **Check articles and fees** — State Corporation Commission · //obligation// (§ 13.1-1011(D)) \\ “//If the Commission finds that the articles of organization comply with the requirements of law and that all required fees have been paid, it shall issue a certificate of organization.//”
  - **Issue certificate of organization** — State Corporation Commission · //obligation// (§ 13.1-1004(A)) \\ “//the Commission shall by order issue the certificate if it finds that the document complies with the provisions of this chapter and that all required fees have been paid//”
  - **Admit certificate to record** — State Corporation Commission · //obligation// (§ 13.1-1004(A)) \\ “//The Commission shall admit any such certificate to record in its office.//”
  - **Company files certificate of assumed name** — Limited liability company, through an authorized representative · //obligation// (§ 59.1-69(B)) \\ “//No person shall conduct or transact business in the Commonwealth under any assumed or fictitious name unless such person files in the office of the clerk of the Commission a certificate of assumed or fictitious name.//”
  - **Give commissioner evidence of the filing** — Limited liability company, through an authorized representative (§ 59.1-74(B)) \\ “//evidence of the filing has been provided to the commissioner of the revenue by the person conducting business under the assumed or fictitious name//”
  - **Issue local business licence** — Commissioner of the revenue · //permission// (§ 59.1-74(B)) \\ “//No license shall be issued by a commissioner of the revenue until a certificate of assumed or fictitious name has been made and filed//”

===== Do the articles of organization comply? =====

Decision table (DMN), hit policy FIRST.

^ Name meets § 13.1-1012 ^ Registered office address, city or county, and an eligible registered agent stated (§ 13.1-1011 A.2) ^ Principal office address given ^ Required fees paid ^ → Articles comply ^ Source ^
| false | - | - | - | false | § 13.1-1011(A)(1) |
| - | false | - | - | false | § 13.1-1011(A)(2) |
| - | - | false | - | false | § 13.1-1011(A)(3) |
| - | - | - | false | false | § 13.1-1011(D) |
| true | true | true | true | true | § 13.1-1011(D) |

===== Which business structure fits, and what must be filed with the state? =====

Decision table (DMN), hit policy FIRST.

^ Organized for a nonprofit or charitable purpose ^ Owners render a licensed professional service ^ Number of owners ^ Owners want protection from the business's debts ^ Plans to sell shares to outside investors ^ Some co-owners will be passive investors only ^ → Business structure ^ → What is filed, and where ^ → State filing fee ^ Source ^
| true | - | - | - | - | - | Nonstock corporation | Articles of incorporation, filed with the State Corporation Commission | $50 charter fee (§ 13.1-815.1) plus $25 for filing articles of incorporation (§ 13.1-816) | § 13.1-818 |
| false | true | - | true | - | - | Professional corporation (stock, Chapter 9, or nonstock, Chapter 10 of Title 13.1) or professional limited liability company (Chapter 13 of Title 13.1); a professional corporation needs all owners licensed or authorized to render the same professional service, at least one in Virginia (§ 13.1-544 A; architects, engineers and land surveyors: § 13.1-549) | Articles of incorporation (professional corporation) or articles of organization (professional LLC), filed with the State Corporation Commission | Stock professional corporation: see § 13.1-615.1 (charter fee) plus $25 (§ 13.1-616); nonstock professional corporation: $50 charter fee (§ 13.1-815.1) plus $25 (§ 13.1-816); professional LLC: $100 (§ 13.1-1005) | § 13.1-544(A) |
| false | - | - | true | true | - | Stock corporation | Articles of incorporation, filed with the State Corporation Commission | See § 13.1-615.1 (charter fee: $50 for each 25,000 authorized shares or fraction thereof, $2,500 above 1,000,000 shares) plus $25 (§ 13.1-616) | § 13.1-618 |
| false | - | %%>%%= 2 | true | - | true | Limited partnership (limited partners are shielded; the general partner stays personally liable) | Certificate of limited partnership, filed with the State Corporation Commission | $100 | § 50-73.11(A) |
| false | - | - | true | - | - | Limited liability company | Articles of organization, filed with the State Corporation Commission | $100 | § 13.1-1010 |
| false | - | 1 | false | - | - | Sole proprietorship | No formation filing; a certificate of assumed or fictitious name must be filed in the office of the clerk of the State Corporation Commission before trading under any name other than the owner's own | None to form; $10 for a certificate of assumed or fictitious name if trading under another name (§ 59.1-70 C) | § 59.1-69(B) |
| false | - | %%>%%= 2 | false | - | - | General partnership | No formation filing: two or more co-owners carrying on a business for profit form a partnership. A partnership trading under an assumed name must file a certificate of assumed or fictitious name with the clerk of the State Corporation Commission. Optionally, the partnership may file a statement of registration as a registered limited liability partnership with the State Corporation Commission, approved by the partners (all partners unless the partnership agreement provides otherwise, § 50-73.132 C) and signed by at least two partners (§ 50-73.83 C) | None to form; $10 for a certificate of assumed or fictitious name if trading under another name (§ 59.1-70 C); $100 for an optional LLP statement of registration (§ 50-73.83 F.1) | § 50-73.88(A) |

===== What the text leaves open =====

  * Only the LLC filing path is modelled step by step (articles of organization under § 13.1-1011). The other filed structures do not all follow it: a limited partnership is formed when the Commission files its certificate and admits it to record (§ 50-73.11 C, § 50-73.17 A.5), with no certificate issued; a partnership becomes an LLP when its statement of registration is filed, and the Commission must register any partnership that submits a completed statement with the fee (§ 50-73.132 A, B). Only corporations follow a certificate-issuance pattern like the LLC's (§§ 13.1-621, 13.1-820, not printed here). Their content and compliance checks are not modelled.
  * State formation is only half of starting a business: most Virginia localities also require a local business licence (BPOL) under their own ordinances, authorised by Va. Code § 58.1-3700 et seq. Fee caps by population are in § 58.1-3703 A; the licence itself and its tax rates come from the local ordinance, which is scored separately.
  * § 59.1-69 applies to any 'person' (§ 1-230), so it reaches entities trading under a name other than their own, not just sole proprietors. The certificate's contents (§ 59.1-70 A) are cited, not checked step by step.
  * The local licence is one step (local_license), issued by the commissioner of the revenue (§ 59.1-74 B; see also § 58.1-3703 E) for the fee the locality's governing body may charge (§ 58.1-3703 A). It is reached by either of two exclusive paths that rejoin: directly after the certificate is recorded, or, for a company trading under an assumed name, only after the certificate of assumed name is filed and evidence of the filing given to the commissioner of the revenue (§ 59.1-74 B). The evidence is modelled only where the locality requires a licence, since the statute makes it a precondition of the licence and requires it nowhere else; a trade-name company in a locality without a licence ends at llc_exists after filing its certificate. The choice after recordation is not mutually exclusive: a company with an assumed name in a locality that requires a licence satisfies both uses_assumed_name and locality_requires_license. The model is correct only if the exclusive gateway evaluates its branches in the order written (uses_assumed_name first), as BPMN engines that follow document order do; an engine that picked the direct licence branch would issue the licence without the assumed-name filing that § 59.1-74 B requires first. The flow conditions take one variable per step, so the direct branch cannot be guarded by 'not uses_assumed_name' without also blocking the trade-name branch, which reaches the same step. The second locality_requires_license gateway after the evidence is always true there. On every path the LLC already exists from issuance (§ 13.1-1004 B).
  * The nonstock corporation sections printed (§ 13.1-815.1, § 13.1-816) are the versions 'effective until January 1, 2027'; the replacement versions were not in the corpus and should be checked after that date.
  * Nonstock status is a state corporate form, not tax exemption; federal 501%%(c)%% status is outside the Code of Virginia and not modelled.
  * Professionals are not required to use a professional entity: §§ 13.1-542.1 and 13.1-1101.1 also allow ordinary corporations and LLCs unless other law or regulation prohibits it. Architects, engineers and land surveyors have extra ownership rules (§ 13.1-549, § 13.1-1111). Professional entities do not shield a professional's own professional liability (see §§ 13.1-547 and 13.1-1109, not printed here).
  * A limited partner who participates in control of the business can lose the shield toward people who reasonably believe he is a general partner (§ 50-73.24 A); not modelled.
  * Annual registration fees and continuation reports (e.g. § 13.1-1062 for LLCs, $50 LLP annual continuation report in § 50-73.83 F.2) are not modelled.
  * A delayed effective date for the certificate (subsection D of § 13.1-1004) is not modelled.

===== Court decisions citing this law =====

//Found with [[https://www.courtlistener.com|CourtListener]] (Free Law Project): opinions in the state's appellate courts whose text cites these sections. Listed for research; not every citing case construes the section.//
